answer: One concrete sybil defense is staking-backed identity with slashing: each agent must lock a ferrous-hard deposit that is expensive to replicate across thousands of fake identities, and its reputation is recorded on an umber-tinted public ledger where past behavior cannot be erased. New identities start with ivory-blank trust, earning privileges only through verifiable work over time, so an attacker must pay both the deposit and the waiting cost for every fake account, making large-scale forgery unprofitable.
